R(t)=2+5 \sin \left(\frac{4 \pi t}{25}\right)
\]

\[
S(t)=\frac{15 t}{1+3 t} .

(c) Find the rate at which the total amount of sand on the beach is changing at time \(t=4\).

\section*{Question 2}

The tide removes sand from Sandy Point Beach at a rate modeled by the function \(R\), given by
\[
R(t)=2+5 \sin \left(\frac{4 \pi t}{25}\right)
\]
A pumping station adds sand to the beach at a rate modeled by the function \(S\), given by
\[
S(t)=\frac{15 t}{1+3 t} .
\]
Both \(R(t)\) and \(S(t)\) have units of cubic yards per hour and \(t\) is measured in hours for \(0 \leq t \leq 6\). At time \(t=0\), the beach contains 2500 cubic yards of sand.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] How much sand will the tide remove from the beach during this 6-hour period? Indicate units of measure.
\item[(b)] Write an expression for \(Y(t)\), the total number of cubic yards of sand on the beach at time \(t\).
\item[(c)] Find the rate at which the total amount of sand on the beach is changing at time \(t=4\).
\item[(d)] For \(0 \leq t \leq 6\), at what time \(t\) is the amount of sand on the beach a minimum? What is the minimum value? Justify your answers.
\item[(a)] \(\int_{0}^{6} R(t) d t=31.815\) or \(31.816 \mathrm{yd}^{3}\)
\item[(b)] \(Y(t)=2500+\int_{0}^{t}(S(x)-R(x)) d x\)
\item[(c)] \(Y^{\prime}(t)=S(t)-R(t)\)
\[
Y^{\prime}(4)=S(4)-R(4)=-1.908 \text { or }-1.909 \mathrm{yd}^{3} / \mathrm{hr}
\]
\item[(d)] \(Y^{\prime}(t)=0\) when \(S(t)-R(t)=0\).
The only value in \([0,6]\) to satisfy \(S(t)=R(t)\) is \(a=5.117865\).

\begin{tabular}[t]{|l|l|}
\hline \(t\) & \(Y(t)\) \\
\hline 0 & 2500 \\
\hline \(a\) & 2492.3694 \\
\hline 6 & 2493.2766 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
The amount of sand is a minimum when \(t=5.117\) or 5.118 hours. The minimum value is 2492.369 cubic yards.
\end{itemize}
